audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as continuation of the whirlwind response: wild goats, deer, wild donkey, wild ox, ostrich, horse, hawk, and eagle. Emphasis on untamed creaturely wisdom and divine care beyond human control.

verses.restored: Do you know the time when the wild goats of the rock give birth? Do you watch the labor of the deer?

familiar.text: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?

modern.text: “Do you know when mountain goats give birth? Have you watched the doe bear her fawn?

original.text: הֲיָדַ֗עְתָּ עֵ֭ת לֶ֣דֶת יַעֲלֵי סָ֑לַע חֹלֵ֖ל אַיָּל֣וֹת תִּשְׁמֹֽר

verses.restored: Can you number the months they fulfill, and do you know the time they give birth?

familiar.text: Canst thou number the months that they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?

modern.text: Can you count the months they are pregnant? Do you know the time they give birth?

original.text: תִּסְפֹּ֣ר יְרָחִ֣ים תְּמַלֶּ֑אנָה וְ֝יָדַ֗עְתָּ עֵ֣ת לִדְתָּֽנָה

verses.restored: They bow down, bring forth their young, and send out their labor pains.

familiar.text: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.

modern.text: They crouch down and bring forth their young; they deliver their newborn.

original.text: תִּ֭כְרַעְנָה יַלְדֵיהֶ֣ן תְּפַלַּ֑חְנָה חֶבְלֵיהֶ֥ם תְּשַׁלַּֽחְנָה

verses.restored: Their young become strong; they grow up in the open; they go out and do not return to them.

familiar.text: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.

modern.text: Their young ones thrive and grow up in the open field; they leave and do not return.

original.text: יַחְלְמ֣וּ בְ֭נֵיהֶם יִרְבּ֣וּ בַבָּ֑ר יָ֝צְא֗וּ וְלֹא שָׁ֥בוּ לָֽמוֹ

verses.restored: Who sent out the wild donkey free, and who loosed the bonds of the swift donkey,

familiar.text: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?

modern.text: Who set the wild donkey free? Who released the swift donkey from the harness?

original.text: מִֽי שִׁלַּ֣ח פֶּ֣רֶא חָפְשִׁ֑י וּמֹסְר֥וֹת עָ֝ר֗וֹד מִ֣י פִתֵּֽחַ

verses.restored: to whom I gave the desert as his house and the salt land as his dwelling?

familiar.text: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings.

modern.text: I made the wilderness his home and the salt flats his dwelling.

original.text: אֲשֶׁר שַׂ֣מְתִּי עֲרָבָ֣ה בֵית֑וֹ וּֽמִשְׁכְּנוֹתָ֥יו מְלֵֽחָה

verses.restored: He laughs at the noise of the city; he does not hear the shouts of the driver.

familiar.text: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver.

modern.text: He scorns the tumult of the city and never hears the shouts of a driver.

original.text: יִ֭שְׂחַק לַהֲמ֣וֹן קִרְיָ֑ה תְּשֻׁא֥וֹת נ֝וֹגֵ֗שׂ לֹ֣א יִשְׁמָֽע

verses.restored: He searches the mountains as his pasture and seeks after every green thing.

familiar.text: The range of the mountains is his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.

modern.text: He roams the mountains for pasture, searching for any green thing.

original.text: יְת֣וּר הָרִ֣ים מִרְעֵ֑הוּ וְאַחַ֖ר כָּל יָר֣וֹק יִדְרֽוֹשׁ

verses.restored: Will the wild ox be willing to serve you? Will he spend the night at your manger?

familiar.text: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?

modern.text: Will the wild ox consent to serve you? Will he stay by your manger at night?

original.text: הֲיֹ֣אבֶה רֵּ֣ים עָבְדֶ֑ךָ אִם יָ֝לִ֗ין עַל אֲבוּסֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Can you bind the wild ox in the furrow with ropes, or will he harrow the valleys after you?

familiar.text: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?

modern.text: Can you hold him to the furrow with a harness? Will he plow the valleys behind you?

original.text: הֲֽתִקְשָׁר רֵ֭ים בְּתֶ֣לֶם עֲבֹת֑וֹ אִם יְשַׂדֵּ֖ד עֲמָקִ֣ים אַחֲרֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Will you trust him because his strength is great, or leave your labor to him?

familiar.text: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?

modern.text: Can you rely on his great strength? Will you leave your hard work to him?

original.text: הֲֽתִבְטַח בּ֭וֹ כִּי רַ֣ב כֹּח֑וֹ וְתַעֲזֹ֖ב אֵלָ֣יו יְגִיעֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Will you trust him to return your seed and gather it to your threshing floor?

familiar.text: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather it into thy barn?

modern.text: Can you trust him to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?

original.text: הֲתַאֲמִ֣ין בּ֭וֹ כִּי ישוב זַרְעֶ֑ךָ וְֽגָרְנְךָ֥ יֶאֱסֹֽף

verses.restored: The wings of the ostrich beat joyfully, but are they the pinions and feathers of covenant-kindness?

familiar.text: Gavest thou the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich?

modern.text: The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but cannot match the pinions and feathers of the stork.

original.text: כְּנַף רְנָנִ֥ים נֶעֱלָ֑סָה אִם אֶ֝בְרָ֗ה חֲסִידָ֥ה וְנֹצָֽה

verses.restored: For she leaves her eggs on the earth and warms them in the dust,

familiar.text: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,

modern.text: For she leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand.

original.text: כִּֽי תַעֲזֹ֣ב לָאָ֣רֶץ בֵּצֶ֑יהָ וְֽעַל עָפָ֥ר תְּחַמֵּֽם

verses.restored: and forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal trample them.

familiar.text: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.

modern.text: She forgets that a foot may crush them, or a wild animal may trample them.

original.text: וַ֭תִּשְׁכַּח כִּי רֶ֣גֶל תְּזוּרֶ֑הָ וְחַיַּ֖ת הַשָּׂדֶ֣ה תְּדוּשֶֽׁהָ

verses.restored: She treats her young harshly, as though they were not hers; her labor is in vain, without fear,

familiar.text: She is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;

modern.text: She treats her young harshly, as if not her own, with no concern that her labor was in vain.

original.text: הִקְשִׁ֣יחַ בָּנֶ֣יהָ לְּלֹא לָ֑הּ לְרִ֖יק יְגִיעָ֣הּ בְּלִי פָֽחַד

verses.restored: because the Divine made her forget wisdom and did not share understanding with her.

familiar.text: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.

modern.text: For God has deprived her of wisdom; He has not endowed her with understanding.

original.text: כִּֽי הִשָּׁ֣הּ אֱל֣וֹהַּ חָכְמָ֑ה וְלֹא חָ֥לַק לָ֝֗הּ בַּבִּינָֽה

verses.restored: When she lifts herself on high, she laughs at horse and rider.

familiar.text: What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.

modern.text: Yet when she proudly spreads her wings, she laughs at the horse and its rider.

original.text: כָּ֭עֵת בַּמָּר֣וֹם תַּמְרִ֑יא תִּֽשְׂחַ֥ק לַ֝סּ֗וּס וּלְרֹֽכְבֽוֹ

verses.restored: Do you give the horse strength? Do you clothe his neck with a mane?

familiar.text: Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?

modern.text: Do you give strength to the horse or adorn his neck with a mane?

original.text: הֲתִתֵּ֣ן לַסּ֣וּס גְּבוּרָ֑ה הֲתַלְבִּ֖ישׁ צַוָּאר֣וֹ רַעְמָֽה

verses.restored: Do you make him leap like the locust? His majestic snorting is terror.

familiar.text: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils is terrible.

modern.text: Do you make him leap like a locust, striking terror with his proud snorting?

original.text: הְֽ֭תַרְעִישֶׁנּוּ כָּאַרְבֶּ֑ה ה֖וֹד נַחְר֣וֹ אֵימָֽה

verses.restored: He paws in the valley and rejoices in strength; he goes out to meet weapons.

familiar.text: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in his strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men.

modern.text: He paws in the valley and rejoices in his strength; he charges into battle.

original.text: יַחְפְּר֣וּ בָ֭עֵמֶק וְיָשִׂ֣ישׂ בְּכֹ֑חַ יֵ֝צֵ֗א לִקְרַאת נָֽשֶׁק

verses.restored: He laughs at fear and is not dismayed; he does not turn back from the sword.

familiar.text: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.

modern.text: He laughs at fear, frightened of nothing; he does not turn back from the sword.

original.text: יִשְׂחַ֣ק לְ֭פַחַד וְלֹ֣א יֵחָ֑ת וְלֹֽא יָ֝שׁ֗וּב מִפְּנֵי חָֽרֶב

verses.restored: Upon him the quiver rattles, the flashing spear and javelin.

familiar.text: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.

modern.text: A quiver rattles at his side, along with a flashing spear and lance.

original.text: עָ֭לָיו תִּרְנֶ֣ה אַשְׁפָּ֑ה לַ֖הַב חֲנִ֣ית וְכִידֽוֹן

verses.restored: With trembling and rage he swallows the ground; he does not stand still when the horn sounds.

familiar.text: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that it is the sound of the trumpet.

modern.text: Trembling with excitement, he devours the distance; he cannot stand still when the ram’s horn sounds.

original.text: בְּרַ֣עַשׁ וְ֭רֹגֶז יְגַמֶּא אָ֑רֶץ וְלֹֽא יַ֝אֲמִ֗ין כִּי ק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר

verses.restored: At the horn he says, Aha! From afar he smells the battle, the thunder of commanders and the shouting.

familiar.text: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

modern.text: At the blast of the horn, he snorts with fervor. He catches the scent of battle from afar— the shouts of captains and the cry of war.

original.text: בְּדֵ֤י שֹׁפָ֨ר יֹ֘אמַ֤ר הֶאָ֗ח וּֽ֭מֵרָחוֹק יָרִ֣יחַ מִלְחָמָ֑ה רַ֥עַם שָׂ֝רִים וּתְרוּעָֽה

verses.restored: Is it by your understanding that the hawk soars and spreads its wings toward the south?

familiar.text: Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, and stretch her wings toward the south?

modern.text: Does the hawk take flight by your understanding and spread his wings toward the south?

original.text: הֲֽ֭מִבִּינָ֣תְךָ יַֽאֲבֶר נֵ֑ץ יִפְרֹ֖שׂ כנפו לְתֵימָֽן

verses.restored: Is it at your mouth that the eagle mounts up and makes its nest on high?

familiar.text: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high?

modern.text: Does the eagle soar at your command and make his nest on high?

original.text: אִם עַל פִּ֭יךָ יַגְבִּ֣יהַּ נָ֑שֶׁר וְ֝כִ֗י יָרִ֥ים קִנּֽוֹ

verses.restored: On the rock he dwells and lodges, on the tooth of the rock and the stronghold.

familiar.text: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.

modern.text: He dwells on a cliff and lodges there; his stronghold is on a rocky crag.

original.text: סֶ֣לַע יִ֭שְׁכֹּן וְיִתְלֹנָ֑ן עַֽל שֶׁן סֶ֝֗לַע וּמְצוּדָֽה

verses.restored: From there he searches for food; his eyes see it from far away.

familiar.text: From thence she seeketh the prey, and her eyes behold afar off.

modern.text: From there he spies out food; his eyes see it from afar.

original.text: מִשָּׁ֥ם חָֽפַר אֹ֑כֶל לְ֝מֵרָח֗וֹק עֵינָ֥יו יַבִּֽיטוּ

verses.restored: His young ones lap up blood, and where the slain are, there he is.

familiar.text: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain are, there is she.

modern.text: His young ones feast on blood; and where the slain are, there he is.”

original.text: ואפרחו יְעַלְעוּ דָ֑ם וּבַאֲשֶׁ֥ר חֲ֝לָלִ֗ים שָׁ֣ם הֽוּא
